mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating impending recession that negates the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production over a 3-month period signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 55% of periods following a triggered 3-month INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand, which will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises and retail sales remain strong during periods of rising unemployment, indicating labor market weakness is not impacting consumer behavior.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Equity market volatility (VIX) declines and credit spreads narrow during periods of high real rates, indicating financial conditions are not tightening despite the Fed's actions.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Homebuilder stocks outperform the broader market and mortgage applications rise during periods of falling housing starts, indicating housing market weakness is not broadly impacting consumer behavior.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows to less than 100,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims decline and labor force participation rises during periods of slow job growth, indicating labor market weakness is not broadly impacting employment.

mechanism_narrative: When real retail sales decline for three consecutive months, it signals a weakening consumer sector that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises and personal savings rates decline during periods of falling retail sales, indicating consumer spending weakness is not broadly impacting the economy.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate exceeds 3% and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals a potential inflation scare that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in higher future interest rates.
failure_condition: Breakeven inflation rates rise and the dollar weakens during periods of high inflation and low policy rates, indicating the market expects the Fed to successfully contain inflation without aggressive rate hikes.
